correctness.rationale: For a named independent base, every forbidden (q+1)-clique in a diagram extending an admissible internal H uses precisely one old vertex. A new diagram is realized over the actual base by universality followed by homogeneity; a labelled finite diagram isolates the complete type, including in elementary extensions. Thus the number of independent old-vertex neighborhood choices is b_q(H)^m. Two q-cliques forbid 2^(r-q+1) - 2^(r-|Q1 union Q2|) subsets, with the minimum precisely when the overlap is q-1. A third clique itself adds a forbidden subset, so equality cannot persist. Edgeless, single-clique, and complete-minus-edge graphs (with extra isolates) realize the three positive bases. All remaining integer bases are at most B2-1. Equal weights within each class and dominance of the largest remaining base prove the stated total variation and rare-event laws at fixed q,r, with positive constants. At r=q+1, two cliques force the single missing edge, and the remaining vertex for a unique clique has at most q-2 neighbors inside it; this verifies all three coefficients including m=0. An independent whole-diagram bit enumeration of K4 avoidance, without using transfer weights, gave 63, 958, 14646 for q=3,r=4,m=0,1,2. The finite checks corroborate but do not prove the general statements.

value.rationale: The quantitative distribution of complete types is not merely their consistency criterion. The sharp second rare-event rate and concentration on a pair of cliques sharing q-1 vertices give a structural description of the exceptional internal graphs across all fixed eligible arities; the critical-arity formula adds an exact enumerative benchmark. The contribution is modest and combinatorial, not a growing-arity or general-base theorem.
